Each Statement is contained within a Block and connects to other code entities through usage or reference relationships. Enables natural queries like “What statements appear in this block?”, “Where does this function return?”, or “Which line declares this variable?”.

Creation.Description: When a function call is detected within a function body (using language-specific captures such as 'call.definition' and 'call.function'), a CALLS edge is established between the caller and callee Function nodes.
Creation.EnrichmentDescription: Represents a function call relationship between two Function nodes — linking the caller to the callee. Derived from language-specific syntax captures (call.definition, call.function). Enables tracing of call hierarchies and runtime dependencies. Natural queries such as “Which functions call this one?”, “What does this function invoke?”, “Show me the call graph for this file.”.

Creation.Description: Each element carries a file context (via the 'file_path' attribute) that is used to establish a DEFINED_IN edge linking the element to its source File node.
Creation.EnrichmentDescription: Represents a definition-location relationship, linking a Function, Type, Namespace, or Variable to the File (or Namespace) where it is defined. Provides traceability of source locations for code navigation, indexing, and symbol lookup. Enables queries like “Where is this function defined?”, “Which file defines this class?”, or “Which namespace declares this variable?”.

Creation.Description: Preprocessor macros (captured with 'macro.definition') are linked to the File node in which they are defined, forming an INCLUDED_IN relationship.
Creation.EnrichmentDescription: Connects a Macro definition to the File that includes or declares it. Facilitates preprocessor dependency tracking, answering queries such as “What macros are defined in this header?” or “Which file includes this macro definition?”.

Definition.To: Namespace, Type, Function, Block, Literal, Statement, or Macro

Creation.Description: This edge models the hierarchical nesting found in source code. For instance, a File node contains Type and Function nodes, while a Type node may contain its member Variables and Functions, and Block nodes contain Statement nodes. The CONTAINS relationship is derived from structural nesting indicated by language-specific captures. When connecting Block to Statement, an 'order' property maintains statement sequence.
Creation.EnrichmentDescription: Models structural containment — one code entity owning or nesting another. Example chains are 'Project -> File -> Type -> Function', 'Function -> Block -> Statement'. Each relationship preserves syntactic hierarchy and execution order when applicable (e.g., via order). Supports natural queries such as “What does this class contain?”, “Which statements belong to this block?”, “What files are part of this project?”.

Creation.Description: Object-oriented inheritance constructs (e.g., 'class.base', 'class.superclass') are mapped to INHERITS_FROM edges, linking derived types with their base types.
Creation.EnrichmentDescription: Represents classical inheritance in object-oriented code, linking a derived Type to its base Type. Enables semantic queries such as “Which classes extend this base class?” or “What is the inheritance tree for this type?”. Useful for structural analysis, polymorphism exploration, and type hierarchy resolution.

Creation.Description: Language constructs indicating interface implementation (such as a class listing interfaces in 'class.base') are normalized into an IMPLEMENTS edge, representing that a type conforms to an interface contract.
Creation.EnrichmentDescription: Represents an interface implementation — where a class or struct conforms to an interface contract. Normalizes constructs like class.base or interface lists across languages. Enables questions such as “Which types implement this interface?” or “Does this class implement IDisposable?”. Supports OOP and dependency-injection graph analysis.

Creation.Description: When a variable declaration is encountered (via captures like 'declaration.definition' or 'field.definition'), a DECLARES edge is created linking the declaration scope to the Variable node, enabling scope-aware queries.
Creation.EnrichmentDescription: Represents the declaration relationship — linking a scope (Function, Type, Namespace, or Block) to Variables defined within it. Enables scope-aware symbol resolution and declaration tracing. Helps in answering common questions like 'Which variables are declared inside this block?', 'What fields belong to this class?', or 'What local variables are declared in this function?'.

Creation.Description: Represents code-level reference relationships among symbols. A REFERENCES edge is established whenever a Function, Type, or Variable refers to another Function, Type, or Variable within source code. This models symbol usage links detected through parsing and semantic analysis, capturing how declarations are used or invoked in code. The edge supports data flow, dependency, and reference resolution analysis, enabling cross-entity connectivity across files and scopes.
Creation.EnrichmentDescription: Represents the same concept as a 'Go to References' or 'Find All References' operation in language server protocols (LSP). This relationship connects where a symbol is declared to all points where it is referenced, used, called, or accessed within the codebase. It provides the semantic link between definitions and their usages, supporting natural queries such as 'Where is this variable used?', 'Which functions reference this type?', 'Show all references to this method?', and 'What code depends on this symbol?'. This edge is essential for dependency visualization, impact analysis, and code navigation experiences that mirror IDE-level cross-references. It bridges semantic understanding (intent of usage) with structural representation (where usage occurs), improving both retrieval precision and interpretability for LLM-driven or natural-language graph exploration.

To reach non-File nodes from Project, traverse through File nodes first. Project config files (.csproj, package.json, pyproject.toml, etc.) are NOT stored as separate File nodes - their contents are extracted and stored as JSON strings in config_metadata and build_properties. Use apoc.convert.fromJsonMap() to parse and query these JSON strings.

Configuration files like .csproj, package.json, or pyproject.toml are not represented as File nodes. Their parsed metadata is instead stored within attributes (config_metadata, build_properties, and dependencies). This node allows for questions such as “What files belong to this project?”, “What is the target framework?”, or “What dependencies are declared?” — supporting structural and metadata-level project analysis.

Helps in answering common questions like 'Which variables are declared inside this block?', 'What fields belong to this class?', or 'What local variables are declared in this function?'.

Creation.Description: Represents code-level reference relationships among symbols. A REFERENCES edge is established whenever a Function, Type, or Variable refers to another Function, Type, or Variable within source code. This models symbol usage links detected through parsing and semantic analysis, capturing how declarations are used or invoked in code. The edge supports data flow, dependency, and reference resolution analysis, enabling cross-entity connectivity across files and scopes.
Creation.EnrichmentDescription: Represents the same concept as a 'Go to References' or 'Find All References' operation in language server protocols (LSP). This relationship connects where a symbol is declared to all points where it is referenced, used, called, or accessed within the codebase. It provides the semantic link between definitions and their usages, supporting natural queries such as 'Where is this variable used?', 'Which functions reference this type?', 'Show all references to this method?', and 'What code depends on this symbol?'. This edge is essential for dependency visualization, impact analysis, and code navigation experiences that mirror IDE-level cross-references. It bridges semantic understanding (intent of usage) with structural representation (where usage occurs), improving both retrieval precision and interpretability for LLM-driven or natural-language graph exploration.
